traps: Calling cosine similarity translation-invariant. It is invariant to positive scaling, not to shifts; centering the batch changes all angles.
Dropping the positive from the denominator. SimCLR sums over k != i, which includes the positive; without it the loss can go negative.
Reading NT-Xent as fixed-class classification. The classes are the current batch views, so the same pair gets a different loss in different batches.
units.why: Contrastive objectives compare directions, not positions. If norms leak into the logits, the loss rewards loud embeddings instead of aligned ones.

focus: Dividing by tau multiplies every logit gap. Small tau sharpens toward argmax; large tau flattens toward uniform.
The positive-logit gradient is -(1 - p_pos)/tau. Easy pairs saturate near zero gradient at small tau, so hard negatives drive learning.
Negatives per positive equal 2(N-1): 510 at batch 256 and 16,382 at batch 8192. Longer training closes much of the batch gap.
Random crop plus color distortion wins because it blocks the color-histogram shortcut, not because either transform is strong alone.
outcomes: Derive the 1/tau sharpening of logits and gradients, and predict saturation at small tau.
Explain how batch size sets the negative count and when longer training closes the gap.

focus: An augmentation declares an invariance. Crop-only declares color histograms fair game, and the encoder takes that shortcut.
Every batch negative is repelled, including same-class images. At batch 8192 with 1000 balanced classes, each anchor repels about 16 same-class views.

SimSiam survives on positives alone because stop-gradient plus predictor break the symmetry that admits the constant solution. Removing either collapses to 0.1 percent.

traps: Probing z instead of h. Rotation accuracy falls from 67.6 to chance because z was trained to forget orientation.

focus: Patchify is a disjoint row-major grid: (H/p) by (W/p) patches, each flattened to C*p^2 values (768 for 3-channel 16px patches).
One convolution with kernel equal to stride equal to patch size does extraction plus projection; D2L output keeps one vector per patch.
Self-attention is permutation-equivariant, so order must be injected. D2L learns pos_embedding from random init; the UDL ViT learns 1D encodings too.
Halving patch size quadruples tokens and multiplies attention work by 16.
outcomes: Implement patch extraction as stride-equals-size convolution and verify count, order and flat dimension.

focus: A^L counts walks, not paths: revisits allowed. The diagonal of A^2 holds node degrees.
Correct layers are permutation-equivariant: permuting node order permutes embeddings identically. Readouts for graph labels must be invariant.
Repeated averaging converges toward the random-walk stationary distribution, so deep stacks wash out local signal.
Two layers are the empirical norm; depth needs residuals, not just more of the same layer.

units.title: Graph message passing and oversmoothing
traps: Counting paths with A^L. Walks may revisit nodes; the book states this explicitly.
Expecting depth to help by default. Mean aggregation converges across nodes, so a 10-layer stack can underperform a 2-layer one.
Indexing nodes as an ordered input. If shuffling IDs changes predictions beyond permutation, the layer is wrong, not the data.
units.why: Graphs make neighborhoods explicit. Each layer trades local identity for wider context, and past a point the averaging erases what made nodes distinct.
